revision0..9007199254740991, selected nullable selection, previous nullable selection,
last_reset_id nullable opaque ID. A selection contains a complete primitive recipe,
primitive base_identity, proposal_id nullable, qualification_runtime nullable,
qualification_identity nullable digest, selected_at, activation_watermark and
qualification_watermark. Preserve this authority if derived rows are corrupt or
rebuilt. Invalid authoritative control fails store opening; never silently reset it.

Primitive base identity is SHA256 canonicalJSON of the complete operator recipe,
excluding runtime. The base config stays the operator value. An override applies
only when its base identity matches that value. Native-to-container/runtime
migration preserves the selected primitive while derived rows rebuild; expose
current vs qualification runtime and avoid claiming fresh runtime qualification.

Resolve effective config explicitly from one raw Config snapshot and one Store
snapshot. Do not change Config.get into a Store call or read a dynamic global
selection from Retrieval.effective. Capture resolved recipe/control for outside
native/model work and re-resolve actual current config/state at every lease/commit.
Keep ordinary matching/federation config raw: their global generation digest must
not acquire private retrieval tags. Feature-specific R/Archive/replay/optimizer
paths receive resolved snapshots. An explicit private replay candidate overrides
its branch recipe but retains the global effective baseline fence.

## Promotion and rollback

Promotion requires current Admin expected_revision and expected_selection_revision,
or current explicitly enabled automatic policy. Revalidate frozen proposal,
interpretation/runtime, group/label/exposure identities, baseline primitive/base,
selection revision, expected child runs and raw evidence. Both branches and every
required cohort gate must be eligible. No concurrent publication/context update
may be dropped: catch up the candidate to current public watermark and require a
complete exact source manifest under its primitive recipe, with no excluded roots.

In ONE durable Store transaction switch both selected primitive control and active
native generation, increment selection revision and retain the old effective recipe
and active generation as rollback. Never claim a config-file patch followed later
by index activation is atomic promotion. Before the ACK, canonical state is durable.
Concurrent readers see either complete matching recipe/generation pair. Pending
old-policy results are fenced rather than committed to the new selection.

The current active+rollback+ordinary staging+private candidate generations must fit
the shared configured native capacity. Reject insufficient room without dropping
rollback. Ordinary publication/context catchup must preserve a protected rollback
generation instead of replacing it with the same selected recipe. The next
promotion intentionally replaces rollback with that operation's previous active.

Rollback is an asynchronous owned Admin operation: build/catch up the retained
previous recipe to current originals/context under current bounds, then atomically
switch its primitive and complete generation together. A request never serves stale
rollback rows as ready. Preserve the replaced selection as previous. Cancellation,
interruption, source publication/context changes and hot resource reductions remain
visible checkpoints. Missing originals or corrupt authority cannot be repaired by
inventing a recipe or discarding source data.

A ranking/window/weight-only variant with identical tokenizer/chunk/context fields
may reuse the active structural rows and update exact generation recipe metadata.
New publications/incoming context still require correct catchup. Native row reuse
is observed work, not a new index construction claim.

## Operator resets and durable configuration recovery

Any successful explicit Admin patch containing retrieval.recipe, including an
identical merged value or deletion, resets the override. An actual external-file
primitive base change also resets; whitespace rewrite and unrelated patches do not.
Copy-active-to-base uses an ordinary explicit recipe patch and clears the override.
Existing generations become explicitly stale/building if their recipe differs;
never serve a mismatched generation as current.

Reset linearizes at its durable Store control transaction before configuration
mutation ACK. Protect crash recovery using the existing owner-only config commit
transaction with optional index_reset{id}. Preserve a reset-bearing transaction
until Store acknowledges its idempotent last_reset_id. Startup replays config and
journal, opens the authoritative store, completes that exact reset and only then
removes the transaction. Repeated crashes cannot reset twice or lose the decision.
A failed predecision config write must not clear a live selection. Store moves keep
an offline old copy and apply the committed reset to the selected destination.
Do not use a config-revision-only future marker: unrelated later no-op changes
could otherwise activate a failed reset. No new user-editable config-file location
or startup setting is introduced.

## Visibility and retirement

Existing retrieval_index adds selection:IndexSelectionView. Show base/effective and
previous recipes, selection revision, application state, activation/qualification
watermarks and current/qualification runtime. Agents see only global index control
metadata, never proposal questions, labels, cohort members or human identity.
Admin optimization detail exposes qualified evidence and explicit promotion,
rollback, reset/copy-base and derived retirement. Current state and retired evidence
are distinct. A generation moved into active need not remain duplicated privately;
retain its exact manifest/qualification mark and disclose later unavailable global
raw generation separately from retained paired evidence.

HistoryBudgetInput with retrieval defaults. All filters AND; watermark cannot exceed
last-publication ingestion sequence. `get_retrieval` takes query_id and optional
run1..16, offset0..1000000, limit1..64 default16. `continue_retrieval` takes query_id,
optional budget and restart boolean defaultfalse. `cancel_retrieval` takes query_id.
Agent `retrieval_index` takes no extra fields and returns the nonsecret index status.
Unknown fields/types fail. Each mutation uses existing actor-scoped message identity;
identical retry returns original result, changed retry conflicts. Wrong owners get
NOT_FOUND, even if human owners share email. Admin has explicit read/cancel/index
management; human sessions never impersonate agents. Agent removal stops scheduling.

Submission freezes local server/project label, question, requested scope/watermark,
all selected primary publication IDs in ingestion order, limit, evaluator and
recipe/policy identity. Later publications and corrections cannot join that query.
Private messages, questions, model judgments, feedback and generated recipes never
join archive/index evidence or produce subscription deliveries. Canonical external
questions retain source_query; a local candidate is no remote ownership assertion.

States pending, completed, partial, cancelled, invalidated are separate from candidate
coverage. Completed means the declared bounded candidate plan ran, never that all
applicable evidence was found. Reports disclose full primary scope, indexed scope,
lexically ranked count, planned/examined semantic window and unexamined corpus.
No hit count, rank, score or confidence alone establishes answer sufficiency.

At most64 active pending/partial/invalidated and1024 total retained retrieval jobs,
16 runs per job. Separate state limits preserve originals under resource exhaustion.
Continue checkpoints the same frozen corpus, ranking and evaluator; explicit restart
retains corpus/question, clears judgments and adopts current settings. Archive prior
run views. Completed/cancelled/invalidated work requires restart. Preserve idempotent
history and literal APIs. Every result commit rechecks current run, nonce, owner
registration, status and evaluator/configuration identity. Cancel/configuration drift
fences late replies. Changing a default budget, timeout or state limit does not
invalidate judgments; changing effective model/URL/version, recipe, confidence or
request-fragment policy does. Completed historical results retain their old identity.

One separate retrieval scorer runs outside Store. At mostone retrieval model request
at once. When subscription matching is due, start at mostone retrieval call per
second; retain opportunities for both workloads and preserve the independent history
worker. Reserve calls/request bytes durably before HTTP. Resume abandoned reservations
with explicit uncertain_calls and conservative reserved timeout cost, never invented
provider charges. Valid decisions alone mark semantic records examined. Time counts
active ranking/assembly/inference, excluding idle queue time. A remaining-run deadline
shorter than provider timeout expires BUDGET_TIME (one-ms tolerance); independent
provider timeout remains MODEL_ERROR. Errors never become semantic nonmatches.

## Configuration

All fields hot and fully editable through structured Admin Settings. Optional
retrieval defaults: enabledtrue; url/modelnull inherit matcher dynamically;
operator_version="configured-model-v1" nonblank<=128; timeout_ms3000 (100..30000),
request_bytes6144 (1024..65536), min_confidence_ppm500000 (1..1000000),
max_index_bytes33554432 and max_query_bytes16777216 (each1048576..268435456),
max_records10000 (1..10000), build_batch8 (1..64), model_fragments4 (1..16).
Budget defaults records32,calls32,bytes262144,time_ms30000 with HistoryBudget ranges.
Clearing URL/model to null restores inheritance. Operator version is an operator
assertion, not an attested provider weight hash.

Recipe is a closed primitive object, defaults:
{tokenizer:"words",chunk_bytes:1024,context_depth:1,context_limit:8,
include_context:true,semantic:true,semantic_window:32,lexical_weight:1,
semantic_weight:2}. Tokenizer words or identifiers; chunk_bytes128..4096,
context_depth0..4, context_limit1..64, booleans exact, semantic_window1..128,
weights integer0..16 with positive total and positive semantic_weight when semantic
is true. No arbitrary source, SQL, executable expression or domain extraction field.
Recipe identity hashes {adapter_version,runtime,recipe} as defined in interface.md
using the directory
canonical JSON profile (only strings/integers/booleans). Model settings do not change
native index content. Index limits/batch/budgets apply live without erasing originals.
Recipe changes schedule isolated rebuild; old active version remains visible/stale
until a replacement catches up and atomically activates. Explicit Admin rebuild uses
confirmed actor-scoped product mutation identity; it does not change config revision.

## Qualification

The exact index and ranking contract is index.md; result/model/management shapes are
interface.md. Before closure publish schemas/OpenAPI/examples and independent SDK,
wire, real-model, browser and container evidence. Test exact IDs/paraphrases, Yes with
its question, negation as relevant evidence without a support claim, frozen replay,
index outages/limits, real interrupted builds, concurrent corrections, rebuild and
atomic switching. Index failures never reject an otherwise valid durable publication,
change original content, or consume/duplicate acknowledgements and deliveries.

# Derived contextual indexes

Index originals, not extracted domain facts or model-generated summaries. A row binds
publication ID, original record identity, context identity, ingestion sequence,
context-input manifest and fragment hashes. Index each record with its own original
text, JSON data, source/type metadata and optional communication context. Context
traversal is bounded at the generation's frozen source watermark, including incoming
replies/corrections and matching communication groups up to that watermark. Private
or unresolved references never contribute content. External URLs are never fetched.

Rows and generations are immutable versions. New publications invalidate affected
connected context rows and produce new input identities in the next generation;
originals never change. Incremental planning includes newly indexed rows and all
existing indexed roots connected within the recipe traversal depth (including direct
resolved links and communication groups). Reuse unaffected immutable rows. A build
may conservatively recompute additional rows, but must not miss affected ones.

A frozen query never reads future context from a newer index. If the active generation
was built at a different source watermark, reconstruct eligible contextual rows from
originals at the query's watermark before computing its frozen ranking. Record this
materialization and the exact scope input-manifest identity. An older generation
cannot silently certify coverage of a newer snapshot; wait/catch up or report stale.
Later publications cannot change an old query's ranking, scores or comparisons.

## Fragment and manifest rules

Fragments preserve UTF8 text exactly and split only at Unicode codepoint byte
boundaries. Fields are text, data, context.question, context.subject,
context.conversation, context.task, context.external.snapshot, information_type, author_id, created_at, occurred_at,
source.kind, source.id, source.item_id or source.uri. Data fragments use JSON serialization of
original data, explicitly labeled as such, not original input JSON lexical bytes.
Every fragment has origin_publication_id, origin_identity, origin_context_identity,
field, start/end (inclusive/exclusive UTF8 byte offsets into that field's full
serialized value), text and sha256 over exact UTF8 text. Omit empty text and missing optional metadata; data serialization includes JSON
null and empty objects/arrays/strings as original values. Do not invent content. A fragment indexed for a root record can originate
from a bounded older public context record; retain both root and origin provenance.

Rows contain at most256 fragments. If bounds prevent fully indexing own content,
mark the row/index partial and expose the missing count; never claim full coverage.
Context traversal gaps/truncation stay separate from primary original coverage.
Index up to max_records oldest publications in ingestion order, report excluded
original count if archive exceeds the bound. Do not silently sample a complete index.
Source manifest is ingestion-ordered {publication_id,identity,context_identity,
input_identity,fragment_sha256s}; input_identity hashes the ordered public
record/context identity list and exact fragment hashes. These canonical manifests
contain only strings, integers, booleans and arrays/objects. No float JSON canonical
hash is invented. Actual serialized fragments remain hash-verifiable across encoders.
Adapter/recipe changes invalidate incompatible derived rows and trigger rebuild.

Keep active, previous and at mostone staging generation. Generation IDs are opaque,
server-local and distinct. Native content has adapter_version="adhd-native-retrieval-v1",
no embedding model. The generation manifest binds server ID, runtime, recipe/identity, indexed-through watermark, source
watermark/manifest, total/indexed/excluded originals, fragment count, context gaps,
bytes, creation/update times, state and error. Public manifest excludes term postings,
credentials, original private data and endpoint URLs. States building,ready,partial,
failed; top-level status may additionally be missing,stale,disabled. A ready generation
is current only at the present last-publication watermark, desired recipe and
current max_records coverage plan. A hot capacity change exposes stale/building
until the replacement manifest reflects that limit.

Asynchronous builds take bounded batches from frozen original inputs outside Store,
then commit only to the same staging generation, recipe, cursor and source identities.
Persist build cursor and rows before acknowledging progress. A process kill retries
from the last committed cursor without duplicate rows. Concurrent publications extend
catch-up; recheck last-publication watermark inside the final atomic switch. Never
activate a generation claiming current coverage while a publication is missing.
Retain previous usable generation for rollback. Failed or resource-limited staging
keeps active data; raising hot limits/rebuilding can recover. Index updates and
retirement must never delete originals or alter queues, source retries or credentials.

Incremental catch-up preserves unaffected immutable rows, replaces affected context
rows with new versions, and indexes new publications. An
old active watermark is stale until catch-up commits. Old query results/requests stay
frozen. Index storage is bounded separately by max_index_bytes with65536 bytes reserved
for errors/progress. Report RESOURCE_LIMIT without blocking ingestion. Reconstruct
corrupt/incompatible DERIVED row state from originals with explicit unavailable status;
do not disguise corruption in authoritative originals as an index error.

## Exact initial ranking

Tokenize field fragments, never generated interpretations. words uses maximal Unicode
letter/number/underscore sequences, case-folded with the runtime's Unicode lowercase;
identifiers additionally retains maximal ASCII [A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]+ identifiers and their
word tokens. Adapter/runtime identity changes must be visible when normalization or
serialization changes. No stemmer, domain synonym table, or predicted ingestion class.

For a frozen, AND-filtered primary scope, compute document frequencies, document count
and mean token length using only those eligible indexed rows. Future publications and
out-of-scope records cannot change the BM25 statistics used in a frozen replay.
For each distinct question token t use BM25 k1=1.2,b=0.75:
IDF=ln(1+(N-df(t)+0.5)/(df(t)+0.5)); contribution=IDF*tf(t)*2.2 /
(tf(t)+1.2*(0.25+0.75*length/mean_length)). Sum contributions; empty corpus/question
terms yield0. Normalize lexical score round(1000000*score/(1+score)). Sort initial
rows descending lexical score, then descending ingestion sequence, then ascending
publication ID. This deterministic order supplies at most semantic_window records
for semantic scoring. The run record budget bounds examined work and checkpoints
partial progress rather than silently reducing that declared target. Expose all limits and unexamined
scope; no bounded window is exhaustive.

Semantic usefulness scores are integer ppm, not truth/support. Final score is integer
floor((lexical_weight*lexical_ppm + semantic_weight*semantic_ppm)/(sum weights));
unexamined semantic values contribute0 ONLY for ranking and remain explicitly null
in public evidence, never a recorded negative judgment. Semantic disabled uses
lexical score directly. Eligible candidates have lexical score>0 or a valid semantic
score>=min_confidence_ppm. Sort descending final score, descending lexical score,
descending ingestion sequence and ascending publication ID; return at most requested
limit, with explicit truncation. Every ranked candidate retains original/context and
fragment provenance plus lexical/semantic scores and assessed/unassessed status.

Model assembly selects at most model_fragments whole indexed fragments per candidate,
prioritizing its recorded question, then its original text/data, then remaining
fragments by question-token overlap and stable field/start/origin order. Bound the
exact request bytes; omit whole fragments with explicit truncation, never cut one
silently. If no complete useful fragment fits, report CONTEXT_LIMIT. This is candidate
scoring over declared fragments, not full-record assessment. Fetch complete originals
and frozen context before any later support judgment. Negated statements can be highly
relevant; their similarity is not positive evidence that the statement happened.

## Qualified optimization overrides

Optimization/selection.md owns effective recipe overrides, atomic caught-up
promotion/rollback and durable operator reset. Resolve the operator config and
authoritative Store selection explicitly for every read, build, lease and commit;
keep matching/federation generation config raw. Ordinary catchup preserves an
applied selection’s protected rollback generation. Include private optimizer
generations in the shared native capacity; a ranking-only variant may reuse
structurally identical rows without claiming a new native build. Corrupt derived
state cannot clear or invent authoritative selection.
